findings.detail: v2 equated the 38 us/day satellite clock offset, a common pseudorange bias (~11 km) and a GPS position error. SRC24 (Misra) says the common bias is absorbed by the receiver clock offset, position unaffected, timing off 38 us/day. Fixed in v3 N03, N19, N19b; ledger C12 revised with a forbidden pattern.

v2 said the message time count 'tells the receiver which repeat'. v3 states the code fixes delay only within 1 ms and that each LNAV 6 s block carries a time-of-week word near its start (SRC14), 50 bps.

v2 let the signal-in-space URE read as phone accuracy. v3 labels URE as the error of one distance and gives the phone figure separately (SRC16, SRC15); 0.643 m is a 95th-percentile bound on one day, not an average.
SRC24 states the 11 km bound applies 'between daily uploads of clock corrections' and under identical circular orbits; v3 adds 'by the next daily clock update' and 'in this simplified picture'.
SRC24 supports 'receivers use inexpensive clocks that drift'; wording restored with that source.

TTS calibration: Kokoro misread 'L2C' (ASR heard 'out to c' / 'altacy'). L5, L1C, WAAS, FAA, NIST need explicit readings in the pronunciation pass before any full TTS. Numbers and technical words (pseudorange, ionosphere, troposphere) were heard correctly.

findings.detail: External review (11/10/2026) asked for: N03/N18 phrased as a counterfactual (without correction), N19b with the identical-circular-orbit assumption first and the position claim limited to that idealized case, N29 stated as the daily global-average URE commitment (95%), not a bound on each signal or on phone position. Applied in v4. Re-QA found the proposed N19b/N29 wording failed 3 deterministic checks (ordinal "ninety-fifth" read as 90, C12 forbidden phrase "position error" in N29, three sentences opening with "The receiver"); N19b and N29 were re-worded against SRC15/SRC16/SRC24 and re-run clean. N29 now says the 2021 figure was "at most about sixty-four centimeters" (source: <= 0.643 m).
